definition: The Nvidia DGX (Deep GPU Xceleration) is a series of servers and workstations designed by Nvidia, primarily geared towards enhancing deep learning applications through the use of general-purpose computing on graphics processing units (GPGPU).
details: These systems typically come in a rackmount format, initially using high-performance x86 server CPUs, switching to ARMs around 2018, and releasing NUCs in 2025. The core feature of a DGX system is its inclusion of 4 to 8 Nvidia Tesla GPU modules, which are housed on an independent system board. These GPUs can be connected either via a version of the SXM socket or a PCIe x16 slot, facilitating flexible integration within the system architecture. To manage the substantial thermal output, DGX units are equipped with heatsinks and fans designed to maintain optimal operating temperatures. Nvidia GPGPUs are featured in TOP500 supercomputers.

explainer.lead: Nvidia DGX is a series of servers and workstations designed by Nvidia mainly for deep learning using general-purpose computing on GPUs. It matters as a turnkey platform for heavy deep-learning workloads.

tiers.eli5: It is a powerful computer built around several graphics chips working together, made for training big models.
tiers.practitioner: Teams deploy DGX systems for multi-GPU training; the pitfall is thermal management, since the tightly packed GPU modules produce substantial heat requiring dedicated cooling.
tiers.paperLevel: A DGX system's core feature is 4 to 8 Nvidia Tesla GPU modules on an independent system board, connected via SXM socket or PCIe x16; formats are typically rackmount, with x86 CPUs initially and ARM around 2018.

explainer.example: A rackmount DGX unit with eight Tesla GPU modules on a dedicated system board trains a model across those GPUs.
